arxiv-2011-14248.title: The 𝔽 p {\mathbb{F}}_{p} -Selberg integral
arxiv-2011-14248.creator: Richárd Rimányi ⋄ and Alexander Varchenko ⋆
arxiv-2011-14248.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Richárd Rimányi ⋄ and Alexander Varchenko ⋆. We prove an 𝔽 p {\mathbb{F}}_{p} -Selberg integral formula, in which the 𝔽 p {\mathbb{F}}_{p} -Selberg integral is an element of the finite field 𝔽 p {\mathbb{F}}_{p} with odd prime number p p of elements. The formula is motivated by analogy between multidimensional hypergeometric solutions of the KZ equations and polynomial solutions of the same equations reduced modulo p p .

arxiv-2109-12752.title: Quantum backreaction on a classical universe
arxiv-2109-12752.creator: Viqar Husain, Suprit Singh
arxiv-2109-12752.description: Abstract We study a first-order formulation for the coupled evolution of a quantum scalar field and a classical Friedmann universe. The model is defined by a state dependent hamiltonian constraint and the time dependent Schrödinger equation for the scalar field.

arxiv-2207-03980.title: Simple master equations for describing driven systems subject to classical non-Markovian noise
arxiv-2207-03980.creator: Peter Groszkowski, Alireza Seif, Jens Koch, A. A. Clerk
arxiv-2207-03980.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Peter Groszkowski, Alireza Seif, Jens Koch, A. A. Clerk. Driven quantum systems subject to non-Markovian noise are typically difficult to model even if the noise is classical. We present a systematic method based on generalized cumulant expansions for deriving a time-local master equation for such systems.

arxiv-2309-12347.title: Transitioning a Project-Based Course between Onsite and Online. An Experience Report
arxiv-2309-12347.creator: Dan Mircea Suciu, Simona Motogna, Arthur-Jozsef Molnar
arxiv-2309-12347.description: Abstract We present an investigation regarding the challenges faced by student teams across four consecutive iterations of a team-focused, project-based course in software engineering. The studied period includes the switch to fully online activities in the spring of 2020, and covers the return to face-to-face teaching two years later.

arxiv-2403-20004.title: Depth from Defocus Technique for High Number Densities and Non-spherical Particles Journal: Measurement
arxiv-2403-20004.creator: Rixin Xu, Zuojie Huang, Wenchao Gong, Wu Zhou, Cameron Tropea
arxiv-2403-20004.description: Abstract The Depth from Defocus (DFD) imaging technique for measuring the size and number concentration of particles in a dispersed two-phase flow has up to now been restricted to relatively sparse particle densities and to identifying only spherical particles. The present study examines two advancements to the technique, widening its range of application significantly.

arxiv-2405-00408.title: Shallow vertex minors, stability, and dependence Thanks: This paper is part of projects that have received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme (grant agreements No 810115 – Dynasnet .
arxiv-2405-00408.creator: Hector Buffière, Eunjung Kim, Patrice Ossona de Mendez
arxiv-2405-00408.description: Abstract . Stability and dependence are model-theoretic notions that have recently proved highly effective in the study of structural and algorithmic properties of hereditary graph classes, and are considered key notions for generalizing to hereditary graph classes the theory of sparsity developed for monotone graph classes (where an essential notion is that of nowhere dense class).

arxiv-2412-03496.title: TRENDy: Temporal Regression of Effective nonlinear Dynamics
arxiv-2412-03496.creator: Matthew Ricci, Guy Pelc, Zoe Piran & \& Noa Moriel, Mor Nitzan
arxiv-2412-03496.description: Abstract Spatiotemporal dynamics pervade the natural sciences, from the morphogen dynamics underlying patterning in animal pigmentation to the protein waves controlling cell division. A central challenge lies in understanding how controllable parameters induce qualitative changes in system behavior called bifurcations.

arxiv-2505-21321.title: Bencher : Simple and Reproducible Benchmarking for Black-Box Optimization
arxiv-2505-21321.creator: Leonard Papenmeier, Luigi Nardi
arxiv-2505-21321.description: Abstract We present Bencher , a modular benchmarking framework for black-box optimization that fundamentally decouples benchmark execution from optimization logic. Unlike prior suites that focus on combining many benchmarks in a single project, Bencher introduces a clean abstraction boundary: each benchmark is isolated in its own virtual Python environment and accessed via a unified, version-agnostic RPC ( RPC ) interface.

pmc-10672309.title: Clinical Trials and Therapeutic Approaches for Healthcare Challenges in Pakistan
pmc-10672309.creator: Aamir Ahmed, Norman R. Williams
pmc-10672309.description: Pakistan faces tremendous challenges in providing healthcare due to a lack of consistent policymaking, increasing expenditure and exponential growth in population since its inception in 1947. These challenges are not just driven by politics, policy and allocation of resources but also by healthcare, environment and characteristics of the population biology.

pmc-11340346.title: Computer-assisted syllable analysis of continuous speech as a measure of child speech disordera)
pmc-11340346.creator: Marisha L Speights, Joel MacAuslan, Suzanne Boyce
pmc-11340346.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In this study, a computer-driven, phoneme-agnostic method was explored for assessing speech disorders (SDs) in children, bypassing traditional labor-intensive phonetic transcription. Using the SpeechMark® automatic syllabic cluster (SC) analysis, which detects sequences of acoustic features that characterize well-formed syllables, 1952 American English utterances of 60 preschoolers were analyzed [16 with speech disorder present (SD-P) and 44 with speech disorder not present (SD-NP)] from two dialectal areas.

pmc-11371399.title: Behavioural Responses of Tropical Bed Bug Cimex hemipterus (F.) (Hemiptera: Cimicidae) to Coloured Harbourage
pmc-11371399.creator: Abd Hafis Abd Rahim, Abdul Hafiz Ab Majid
pmc-11371399.description: Population of the tropical bed bug Cimex hemipterus (F.) (Hemiptera: Cimicidae), a temporary ectoparasite on both humans and animals, have surged in many tropical countries. Tropical bed bugs preferences when selecting a suitable harbourage and oviposition site were investigated. Two-choice and three choice colour assays were conducted to determine whether bed bugs will choose black, red or white coloured harbourages.

pmc-11695471.title: Genetic Landscape and Clinical Manifestations of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1 in a Korean Cohort: A Multicenter Retrospective Analysis
pmc-11695471.creator: Boram Kim, Seung Hun Lee, Chang Ho Ahn, Han Na Jang, Sung Im Cho, Jee-Soo Lee, Yu-Mi Lee, Su-Jin Kim, Tae-Yon Sung, Kyu Eun Lee, Woochang Lee, Jung-Min Koh, Moon-Woo Seong, Jung Hee Kim
pmc-11695471.description: Background Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by tumors in multiple endocrine organs, caused by variants in the MEN1 gene. This study analyzed the clinical and genetic features of MEN1 in a Korean cohort, identifying prevalent manifestations and genetic variants, including novel variants.

pmc-12504307.title: Micronutrient inadequacy in Europe: the overlooked role of food supplements in health resilience
pmc-12504307.creator: Samantha Christie, David Crooks, Rowena Thomson-Selibowitz, Ashley Green-Woolard, Konstantinos Mantantzis
pmc-12504307.description: Micronutrient inadequacy is a significant issue in Europe, partly driven by an evolving food landscape. Food supplements play a critical role in offsetting these gaps, particularly in vulnerable groups, and contribute to the overall health resilience, wellbeing, and productivity across the life-course and population.

pmc-13150307.title: The structure of intact and active Photosystem II from Arabidopsis thaliana at 2.44 Å resolution
pmc-13150307.creator: Jack Forsman, André T. Graça, Abuzer Orkun Aydin, Michael Hall, Rana Hussein, Wolfgang P. Schröder, Johannes Messinger
pmc-13150307.description: Summary Photosystem II (PS II) is a large membrane‐bound protein complex that catalyses light‐driven water oxidation in plants and cyanobacteria. The structure of PS II is well studied in cyanobacteria; however, there are very few PS II structures from plants.

pmc-13253840.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps in tumor microenvironment for radiotherapy: friend or foe?
pmc-13253840.creator: Xuan Luo, Xin Qi, Xiaojia Chang, Zhicheng Wang, Rongrong Liu, Hongguang Zhao
pmc-13253840.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are chromatin-protein complexes released by neutrophils that have dual roles in the tumor microenvironment (TME), participating in anti-tumor immunity and driving malignant progression by promoting tumor proliferation, metastasis, and immune escape. Radiotherapy (RT) exerts anticancer effects by inducing DNA damage and microenvironmental remodeling, but the inflammatory response it triggers can activate the formation of NETs, which exacerbate radioresistance by degrading the extracellular matrix, encapsulating circulating tumor cells, inhibiting CD8+ T-cell infiltration, and promoting distant tumor metastasis.
